msg: Foundation green: Godot 4.7.1, deterministic 20Hz sim, harness produces state.json + metrics.csv + real screenshots
Phase A launched: 7 agents building grid, climate, heat, build+blueprints, render, camera, test rig

P09 climate: 20Hz day arc (dawn->deep night, 9600 ticks exact), lagged temperature model, seeded weather planned a day ahead, and a fixed Great Frost calendar that telegraphs each storm four times before it drops ambient ~12C and heat loss to 2.5x — 129 assertions green, replay byte-identical
Host crashed mid-run; all builder code recovered from disk and committed (24.7k lines, build runs clean exit 0). Resumed at audit stage. Autosave every 3 min now active.

Integration pass: the build is a GAME. boot.tscn assembles world+renderer+GameCamera+build mode; a plain run shows a frozen caldera, a lit hearth, heat pipes, housing with lit windows, warm light pooling on snow at night and a visible day arc. Fixed the seams nobody had joined: heat.heat_sources_for_view (lights were mathematically impossible), climate.phase_progress (the day grade had never been rendered), heat<->build negative caching (1500 walls = 28ms/tick). Real sim bugs fixed and covered: flow-field diagonal corner-cut repair (55/60 placements diverged -> 0), disabled/frozen conduits now carry nothing, heat route cache keys on every routing gate, is_free border ring, speed_scale on walls, blueprint rotation of non-turnable buildings. tools/check.sh is GREEN and proven able to go RED (two injected regressions). Test discovery hid 2480 lines incl. 17 real failures; all 4 standalone suites now run (build 384, camera 526, grid 425, climate 129) plus a new 16-test heat suite. Scenarios regenerated by tools/gen_scenarios.py: no more commands to systems that do not exist. stress_1000 is 1717 buildings on one 1429-node heat grid at 46 ticks/s - HeatFlow's fill is the next perf ceiling. Visual proof: artifacts/integrate/shots (7 frames, first_night).
Round 1 critic verdict: 3.8/10. Heat solver praised as deeper than Frostpunk's. Biggest gap = legibility: rich sim data, zero pixels. Phase B launching with 12 builders.

[P07] Combat landed: 10 enemy defs + 6 weapon defs (game/content/enemies, game/content/weapons), CombatSystem order 80. Structure-of-arrays swarm: 600 bodies at 1.00 ms/tick mean, 1.09 ms worst (design target 2 ms, budget 50 ms), measured by tests/combat/test_combat_scale.gd. Own AssaultField: a second cost surface where a wall costs 34 instead of infinity, so a sealed city gets dug at its weakest panel, a damaged panel gets cheaper (weak points), and an open gate is the cheapest way in; lazily built (~90 ms once, prepared 45 s before dusk), version-gated slice repair, so scenarios without combat pay zero. TurretBattery: every shot spends heat out of a magazine charged at exactly HeatSystem.served_of() - an unheated mount fires 3 shots and is a decoration, proven end to end in tests. 5 targeting policies, real turn rate, per-gun idle reason (no_heat/no_ammo/turning/reloading/no_target/offline) = the combat half of the legibility fix. Weapon refit per mount via meta.weapon. Ammo via P03 withdraw+request_items, unlimited when the round does not exist yet. P08 handoff live: spawn_group/spawn_enemy/wave_status/live_enemy_count; the fallback director stands down on the first external spawn. 54 combat tests / 335 asserts green, replay byte-identical, sim lint clean, first_night 0 errors. Demo run: tests/combat/combat_siege.json -> artifacts/p07_siege (192 kills, 20171 damage dealt, 1241 heat spent on defence, turret_uptime 1.0 -> 0.80 as the grid degrades).

[P10] Research & Progression: 45-node DAG (6 branches, 54 edges, 7 roots, laid out 6x15) in game/content/research/, ResearchSystem order 90. The deliverable is PACING, not the list: every node declares the measured problem it answers, and ResearchPacing measures 20 of them from the live world (heat totals + per-tile bottleneck attribution, climate ambient/storm/visibility, [P08]'s enemy roster for the armoured/swarm share, [P11] census, [P06] discontent) and ranks by signal x stake. first_night reads as a conversation: 'Insulated Clothing - the plain outside is lethal, -27 C' -> 'Field Medicine - people are dying' -> 'Hand Carts - 19 sites waiting on hands' -> 'Belt Drives - 7 machines to keep fed' -> 'Underground Belts - 146 conduit tiles crossing 5 machines' -> 'Draught Sealing - 6 buildings frozen solid'. economy_60min: 16 nodes across 5 branches, incl. 'Pressurised Mains - one tile at 131,130 is throttling 5 buildings' (the heat solver's attribution finally reaching a decision). Costs are paid in 4 instalments from the SAME yard construction eats from, a shortfall stalls with the missing item named, parked work is never lost. The engineers never sign a law: the desperate branch is player-consent only, offered as an 'alternative' when the honest branches have run out. tree_layout() ships positioned nodes+edges+state+reasons for [P18]. Also opened 4 orphaned gates other parts invented (belt_gearing, driven_rollers, thermal_assembly, electrotechnics) - that content was unreachable. Perf: 2.5 us/tick mid-campaign, 13.2 us/tick at 1515 buildings (0.026% of the 50 ms budget). 59 tests / 1182 asserts green, 0 log errors over 11k and 72k tick runs. WARNING FOR EVERY PART: Array.sort() on StringName keys sorts by POINTER, not text - Registry.ids() is not alphabetical and neither was anything sorting StringName keys. Fixed inside game/sim/research via ResearchDefs.sorted_names().

[P13] Rendering, second pass. Every defect the visual critic named was structural, so the structures went. (1)+(2) TERRAIN: the four-baked-tile atlas and the three TileMapLayers are deleted. The ground is now ONE quad with game/view/render/terrain.gdshader over a 115 KB data plane (LcnTerrainField: kind 1 texel/tile, snow/heat/soot 1/2, city presence 1/8). No tile exists to repeat and no chunk exists to seam - the old hard seams were snow baked INTO a tile at the moment its chunk loaded. Terrain-kind boundaries are sampled through a two-octave noise warp and snow coverage is a threshold against world-space noise plus a frost dusting, so the caldera edge is drift lobes and fingers at every zoom instead of a staircase. Full-map ground rebuild 256x256: 196.9 ms -> 2.5 ms. (3) NIGHT: radiator lights were pure white because the LIGHT cookie was the glow sprite (hot flat core); there is now a real 1/(1+kd^2) falloff cookie, heat_light_color tops out at amber not cream, and energy 0.55 -> 0.34. The CanvasModulate has stopped being the darkening mechanism (it was 0.115 luminance at deep night = the void); darkness is made PER SURFACE by a light rig in LcnPalette that the ground shader and the entity tint both evaluate, with a snow-bounce term that exists only over the city and a `wild` term that darkens the plain beyond it. (4) DUSK: grades carry sun_dir + sun_height + sun_col/sky_col. A dusk key at elevation 0.16 GRAZES the plain, so lit drift crests go copper and troughs stay blue - it reads as light falling on things, not a filter over the frame. (5) SILHOUETTES: 7 new archetypes (hearth/radiator/accumulator/silo/kitchen/drill/collector), depot redrawn as an open crate yard with a gantry, 26 total; sprites are baked AT their footprint with sublinear lift, so the 5x5 Hearth is no longer the 3x3 generator blown up 1.67x. housing_block had never matched 'house' and was drawn as a workshop. Enforced by a test that rasterises alpha masks at a COMMON world scale and fails if any pair exceeds 0.82 IoU. (6) PERF, measured not projected: reference first_night at 214 visible buildings went 140.4 ms -> 4.3 ms per frame, entity draw 37.3 ms -> 2.4 ms, 797 -> 239 draw calls. Stress city (1700 structures, ALL 1581 on-screen at once, tests/render/render_perf.tscn, windowed M3 Max): collect 1.2 ms, ground 1.0 ms, entity draw 4.7 ms, EIGHT draw calls - against the critic's ~300 ms projection. Fixes: one sprite atlas for every pass, packed parallel arrays instead of a Dictionary per visible building, a native packed-key sort instead of sort_custom lambdas, LOD cutoffs, lazy light buckets, and a saturation early-out that makes heat/soot stamping cost the district's AREA rather than its building count. Also added: snow accumulation read straight from [P01]'s chunk bytes (climate.snow 0 -> 0.21 over first_night), soot haloes around industry, and a heat shimmer in post that bends what is behind hot air. 31 render tests + the stress suite green; determinism replay byte-identical; first_night visual run 0 errors. Frames: artifacts/p13_art/shots (lenses+HUD off, judge the art) and artifacts/p13_full/shots (as it ships); art sheets in artifacts/P13/art. NOTE FOR THE INTEGRATOR: tools/check.sh is RED for reasons outside [P13] - 5 logistics + 1 core-contract in-process failures, 1 build salvage-rounding failure, and the stress_1000 perf gate at 34 vs a floor of 35 measured while ~20 other Godot processes were saturating the machine (that gate is headless, where LcnViewBootstrap never installs a renderer at all - 0 [render] lines in artifacts/perf/*/log.txt).

P06 society: hope and discontent as a REASON LEDGER, not two floats. Every point of movement is attributed to a named force with a sentence carrying this run's numbers ("Eleven of nineteen homes are below twelve degrees, the coldest is at -9"), a live rate per hour, and what it has cost today and all run; a test asserts the reasons sum exactly to the bar even when it is clamped, and a solved problem stops reporting a rate. Hope has an EARNED CEILING: comfort holds a floor, only events (a night survived, a wave held, a promise kept) buy the rest, and the rest leaks back. Book of Laws: 31 authored pages across a shared trunk plus Order and Faith, with prerequisites, TRANSITIVE foreclosure (committing to one path visibly greys the whole other branch), an 18h seal and per-law debate hours. Laws are not panel numbers: they push work_hours / child_labour / elder_labour straight into [P05] citizens through the surface it exposed, and two tests prove the wire is live. Six overlapping factions form grievances with hysteresis, issue demands with deadlines and checkable terms, and radicalise when failed. Three endings (exile, despair, extinction), each telegraphed by a four rung ladder capped at one rung per sample so no single shock can skip the warnings, with a survivable 12h countdown. 68 tests / 487 asserts green, 0.112 ms/tick at 1517 buildings, society state byte-identical across two separate processes. FOUND A REPO-WIDE DETERMINISM TRAP: Array.sort() on StringName sorts by interned POINTER, not alphabetically, so Registry.ids() and ~116 other sorts in game/sim are order-unstable; it cost two identical seeded runs their determinism until every sort in society/ was moved to an explicit String comparator. Also found: HeatSystem sets `order` in setup(), which runs AFTER Sim sorts, so heat is currently ticking at position 25 BETWEEN production(40) and citizens(50) instead of before logistics.

P08 threat director: nights are COMPOSED, not picked. budget = authored curve x drama x era x heat-signature x adaptation, and every one of those five terms ships as a sentence in next_wave_preview().reasons. Set pieces are dragged onto [P09]'s Great Frost calendar by rule (nights 3/7/12/18/25/33 = First Frost/Second Frost/Deepfall/Silent Storm/Great Frost/Nightfall, all storm_synced), the night after each is a measured false lull. Four-rung telegraph before every night, precision climbing direction -> named roads -> roles -> exact counts, plus a full extra day of notice before a set piece; what is promised at 0:15 is byte-identically what walks in at 0:00 (tested). Vectors are [P01]'s real approach lanes scored by what the player actually built, turrets weighted by the heat [P02] is delivering to them, so a cold turret is a decoration; the main road is the fastest road and the probe is the weakest flank, share-capped at 0.72. Adaptation band is 0.80..1.25, declared in metrics/serialize/preview, relief 1.6x faster than punishment. Consumes [P07]'s roster through a duck-typed adapter instead of shipping a second one, drives it through spawn_group(), and derives the night's outcome from combat's monotonic counters because wave_status() reports live=0 for a wave with six hounds on the road. Ships a full siege model for builds without [P07]. 96k-tick run: 10 nights, 8 -> 245 budget, 6 -> 164 bodies, 1 -> 4 vectors, pressure 1.000 -> 0.900 -> 0.912, zero errors. Own cost 3.4-7.7 us/tick avg at reference scale, 0.53 ms worst tick; 4-20 us at 1717-building stress with a 1.5 ms lane rescan every 5 s. 66 tests / 2014 asserts green, determinism replay byte-identical.

[P04] Production & Recipes: 12 recipes in game/content/recipes/ (RecipeDef, class_name, Registry-scanned), ProductionSystem order 40, plus 3 machines of its own in game/content/buildings/ (recuperator, rubble_sorter, assembly_hall). THE CHAIN IS 5 DEEP and the ratios are the point: scrap -> iron_ore -> iron_plate -> steel_plate -> pipe_segment -> heat_core, tuned so every headline ratio is a whole number - 1 drill feeds 1 smelter (0.80 ore/s exactly), 1 iron smelter feeds 1 steel smelter, 1 iron smelter feeds 1 gear shop, 1 steel smelter feeds 1 pipe shop, and the top of the tree is a deliberate 2:1. ProdRecipeBook.describe_ratios() regenerates that table from the live .tres so a balance pass can diff text instead of re-deriving arithmetic; tests/production asserts the six clean ratios to 0.0005. THE BYPRODUCT LOOP CLOSES: iron smelting cannot be run without producing slag (1 per plate, not optional), and slag has exactly ONE use - insulation - at exactly the rate one smelter makes it, so 1 drill : 1 smelter : 1 gear shop : 1 insulation shop is a block that consumes nothing it does not use. THE HEAT-RECOVERY LOOP needed ZERO heat-side code: a recipe declares waste_heat, the machine banks it, and a RECUPERATOR within 4 tiles drains those banks and hands them to [P02] through the existing deliver_fuel() contract as the pseudo-item 'waste_heat' - heat burns it like coal and never learns where it came from. Uncaptured waste decays at 35%/s, so packing smelters around a recuperator buys 15 heat/s for no coal and sprawling buys nothing. WARMTH COUPLING is per RECIPE, not per building: felt_c = HeatSystem.temperature_at(cell) + insulation*30, and each recipe carries its own min_temperature_c with a 14 C ramp above it - steel stops at -12, circuits at -8, gears keep going to -25. A Great Frost therefore kills the delicate work first and leaves the crude work running, and switching a frozen shop from pipe_segment to gear visibly restarts it (tested). HEAT COST is a rate comparison, not a tax: heat_cost/duration vs def.heat_consumed * HeatSystem.power_factor(), so steel_plate (14 u/s against a smelter's 14 u/s rating) slows exactly 1:1 with a brownout while copper_coil (9.6 u/s) shrugs it off - proven by hanging 14 radiators on the same spur until the solver sheds industry. LEGIBILITY: 11 stall reasons on Bus.machine_stalled (no_recipe/locked/missing_input/output_full/no_heat/too_cold/frozen/unstaffed/depleted/disabled), stall_of(id) returns the reason AND the item AND rate/power/cold/heat_factor/staffing/felt_c, and stalled_machines() returns the whole city's list severity-ranked with world positions - that is [P19]'s overlay in one call. A worked-out seam also raises Bus.alert_raised(1, 'seam_depleted'). Store: production does NOT claim [P11]'s stock provider; ProdStore is a client facade over BuildSystem.stock, so the plates the factory makes are the plates construction spends, and it follows [P03] automatically when logistics claims the ledger. request_fuel/offer_input/take_output/accept_output contracts implemented. PERF: 33 machines cost 155-172 us/tick (0.34% of the 50 ms budget), measured by timing 400 real step() calls; on a 1000-building base with zero machines the A/B delta is ~0.12 ms/tick. The [P11] rescan is a FIXED 10-tick cadence with a one-reflective-read fast path and removals detected from our side (tens of ids, not thousands) - keying it on building count made it a full walk every tick during a build spree. 44 tests / 240 asserts green; determinism byte-identical across two processes on smoke, determinism and first_night; first_night 11k ticks with 0 errors; perf gate green at 36 ticks/s. FOUND, NOT MINE TO FIX: (1) HeatSystem sets `order` in setup(), which runs AFTER Sim sorts, so heat ticks at effective order 50 - behind logistics(30) and production(40) - and test_core_contracts::test_systems_tick_in_declared_order is red for it. One line fixes it: `func _init() -> void: order = SYSTEM_ORDER`, the way build/logistics/production/citizens all do it. Consequence today: machines read last tick's power_factor. (2) HeatFlow seeds its BFS from every live source, so a building that both produces and consumes heat is its own island as a consumer and can never draw the rest from the grid. The smelter (heat_produced 4.0, heat_consumed 14.0) therefore runs at 27% forever, and heat's own bottleneck attribution names it exactly: {node: <itself>, reason: 'supply', load: 4.0}. Every smelter in the game is affected. (3) Confirming [P06]: Array.sort() on StringName orders by intern POINTER; every such sort in game/sim/production now goes through ProdSort. REQUEST TO [P11]: the 3 machines I added are hand-authored .tres, not in tests/build/author_buildings.gd - fold recuperator/rubble_sorter/assembly_hall into your authoring script when convenient, and consider gating assembly_hall behind an unlock_id once [P10]'s tree is stable (I left it open so it is testable). NOTE FOR [P05]: production reads staffing_of(building_id); machines with workers_required > 0 genuinely stop when the shift goes home, which is why the reference run's workshop reads 'unstaffed' at night. Content: game/content/recipes/*.tres regenerate from tests/production/author_content.gd.

P12 Economy & Balance: the difficulty curve is now a measured contract. game/content/economy/ holds a BalanceTable (materials, starting stock, deposit yields, population, research + defence envelopes, audit bands) and a DifficultyCurve that states the intended experience of days 1-7 as bands a run is graded against. tools/analyze_balance.py reads a metrics.csv + state.json and grades every night; economy_60min now passes ALL SEVEN graded days on one heat network with zero errors (day 1 margin 0.94/trough 0.68, First Frost day 3 0.85/0.73 at -38C, Second Frost day 7 0.54/0.36 at -54C with the buffer floor at 0.000). Found and fixed the reason economy_60min was measuring nothing: HeatGraph links two buildings only when one CONDUCTS, so all 16 of its generators sat on private one-node networks, froze, and left supply pinned at the Hearth's 120 for an hour with a green exit code. Also derived THE WARMTH-COVER LAW from a run (a generator holds itself at outside+11C and freezes at -10C, so it dies outside a radiator's field once the plain passes -32C) - 13 of 14 generators were frozen at the final tick before districts became radiator-first. Balance.audit() fences [P11]'s building economy, audit_research() prices [P10]'s tree, audit_threat() checks [P08]'s curve against what the city can arm; all three clean, and 6 deliberately-broken defs prove the fence has teeth. 50 tests / 222 asserts green, sim lint clean, determinism identical, perf gate 37 t/s. OPEN, not mine: the food chain never feeds the city (whole population dies day 4 in every long run despite stocked grain), and first_night's turrets ask for a weapon 'burner_cannon' that does not exist, so a drift_hound eats the Hearth at tick 10531. See game/content/economy/BALANCE.md.

[P04] addendum (same session, after the first entry): (1) DEMO RUN shipped - tests/production/production_chain.json -> artifacts/p04_chain. A whole factory instead of the two machines first_night happens to place: 3 smelters (iron/copper/steel), 2 workshops (gears, and the slag-fed insulation line), an assembly hall on ammunition, a rubble sorter, a recuperator standing between two of the three smelters, and two ore drills on real seams with their own generators and pipes. 9000 ticks, 0 errors, 549 ticks/s, 371 crafts, 11 distinct items, chain depth 4 of 5 reached. Mid-run (t4500) the measured throughput IS the design table: gear 12.0/min (recipe promises 12.0), stone 24.0/min and timber 12.0/min from one sorter (recipe says 2:1), iron_ore 60.1/min, ammo_shell 26.7/min. The recuperator is DELIBERATELY 6 tiles from the iron smelter and 2 from the other two, so the run ends with waste_recovered 1.05 u/s and waste_vented 2.11 u/s - two thirds of the factory's waste heat going up the chimney because of where one building was put. That is the layout lesson in one number pair. (2) FIXED A COLD-START FLAW IN MY OWN DESIGN that only a long run showed: a recuperator that only ever GIVES heat produces nothing before the first smelter beside it finishes a craft, so it cooled and froze solid, and a frozen burner refuses fuel forever. It now also DRAWS a trickle (heat_consumed 2.0) with a 90-unit buffer and insulation 0.8: while producing it covers that itself, and while starved it is not a live source so [P02]'s router can reach it and keep it above freezing. Recovered heat went 0.0 -> 1.05 u/s over the same scenario. (3) Confirmed the two [P02] findings from the first entry ON A RUN, not by reading: in the demo the steel smelter sits at power 0.00 / reason 'no_heat' and the iron and copper smelters at 0.24 and 0.18 rate, all three because a building that both produces and consumes heat is its own island in HeatFlow's BFS. (4) Re-verified after every change: 44 tests / 240 asserts green, first_night 11000 ticks 0 errors, determinism byte-identical across two processes on smoke + determinism + first_night, sim lint clean, perf gate GREEN (stress_1000 39 ticks/s against a floor of 35 - the 33 I measured earlier was ~20 other Godot processes saturating the box, not production; A/B with production removed is within noise). (5) tools/check.sh is RED for exactly one in-process failure, and it is NOT [P04]: test_core_contracts::test_systems_tick_in_declared_order. PROVEN by deleting production_system.gd and re-running that single test - it still fails, a=25 b=30. HeatSystem is the only sim system that sets `order` in setup() instead of _init(), and Sim sorts BEFORE setup() runs, so heat sorts as the default 50 and ticks behind logistics(30) and production(40). One line fixes it. The standalone build suite is also red on a pre-existing salvage-rounding check (55 timber at 55% returns 44, got 214 want 224) that has nothing to do with production; [P11]'s 'definitions load and validate' passes with my three new .tres in it.

title: Readability overlays
summary: Six world-space lenses plus an always-on status layer that surface the heat solver's own analysis: per-network hue+dash, solver-derived flow direction, per-tile bottleneck attribution with leader lines, a marching-squares survival isotherm over the warmth field, per-building freeze countdowns, belt/fuel/stall reads and turret+crew coverage. Self-installs from game/content/overlays/overlay_bootstrap.tres, draws on a follow-viewport CanvasLayer above [P13]'s post stack, and is skipped entirely on headless runs.
hotkeys: F1-F3 + 4/5/6 (a bare number key is claimed only when InputMap says it is free), ALT+1..6, ALT held = detail

perf.note: view-side only; the sim tick budget is untouched

verified: godot --visual --scenario=first_night --out=artifacts/P19 -> 7 shots, 0 SCRIPT ERROR, every lens photographed
tests/overlays 59 passed / 618 asserts, including a 100-sample read-only proof against a serialized world
contracts: GameCamera.set_overlay_modes + overlay_requested are wired, so [P16]'s F1..F5 drive the lenses
duck-typed reads only for [P03]/[P04]/[P05]/[P07]; each lens says so on screen when a system is absent
gaps: belt saturation drawing is exercised against [P03]'s belts_for_view() contract but not yet screenshotted with a large belt network
no gamepad binding for the lenses; keyboard and mouse only
